paragraphs: Two years ago the city of Marlow removed the meters from the parking spaces along its central shopping street, arguing that the fees were driving shoppers to suburban malls. Since then, sales tax receipts from businesses on the street have risen by 18 percent, while receipts from the rest of the city have risen by only 6 percent. The city council has concluded that free parking revived the street's commerce, and it now proposes removing the meters from three other districts. Critics object that the free spaces are occupied from early morning until evening, largely by commuters, but the council answers that the sales figures speak for themselves.
